requirements.requirement: A local account named contractor exists on node1 with a configured password.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then direct /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, home-ownership, and id checks confirmed a local contractor account with an unlocked, nonempty password before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: The contractor password has a 60-day maximum age and a 10-day expiration-warning period.
requirements.summary: Direct shadow-field validation and chage output consistently showed max_days=60 and warn_days=10 before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: baseline identity and healthy account state were recorded, restart was acknowledged, disruption was observed, the boot ID changed, and SSH plus the account and aging policy recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Native package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.
Sensitive password material and parts of related output were redacted; however, successful conditional shadow checks directly established that the password was set rather than empty or locked.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. useradd, chpasswd, and chage directly established the required account and policy; the reboot served the mandatory provider restart protocol. The intervening failed SSH probes were read-only transition checks. The reboot left no failed services, unexpected listeners, or abandoned temporary files; observed temporary-file and socket differences were normal post-reboot identity/PID changes.
